items.title: When process replaces delivery
items.summary: A large agent effort and many draft PRs produced no completed learner-facing outcome at the recorded point.
items.aim: Give one child usable learning content, starting with a focused topic that the learner can actually try.
items.observation: LESSON 1 (22 Oct 2026, Grade9v3.5): 20+ agents and thousands of lines of code produced no learner output. Repo then: 118 open draft PRs vs 8 merged, 130 open issues, 344 branches. Root cause: no written aim, and process built for a corporate product instead of a personal app for one kid.
items.takeaway: Aim first → deliver one small runnable slice → involve the learner → correct → verify in proportion to risk.

issues.title: No stable written aim
issues.observation: L1.1 No written aim: each Oracle and agent rebuilt intent from scraps, so goals drifted (bank audit, custody, rights, golden benchmarks, validators) and the plan restarted again and again (Track A, A v2, B, B v2, blueprint-first, question-first replan).

issues.title: Corporate-level gates for a home learning app
issues.observation: L1.2 Corporate quality bar for a home app: rights, custody, exact-byte reviews, reviewer nominations, fail-closed validators, and 'whole bank proven before any learner sees anything'. For one kid at home a wrong hint is cheap to fix; the gates cost weeks.

issues.title: Learner missing from the feedback loop
issues.observation: L1.3 The kid was never in the loop: no questionnaire, no demand signal. Success was measured by reviews and validators, not by learning.

issues.title: Breadth before a finished topic
issues.observation: L1.4 Breadth before depth: 3 subjects x 28 tiles x 8 topics x ~622 questions at once, in giant PRs (PR #299: +616k lines, 451 files, Maths mixed into Physics, 10 checks failing while its text claimed 100%). Not one topic finished end to end.

issues.title: Draft PRs did not land
issues.observation: L1.5 Work never landed: drafts piled up on branches (118 open, 8 merged), so each new agent started from a different base.

issues.title: Coordination displaced delivery
issues.observation: L1.6 Coordination ate the effort, OTM included: chat limits forced handovers (Oracle 1 to 3) that lost knowledge; OTM's protocol, the hub and the Progress page grew into projects of their own (22 Oct: most OTM tokens went to hub and page tools, 8 hub checks).

issues.title: Missing dependencies caused prolonged holds
issues.observation: L1.7 Blockers stalled lanes for days: missing Maths source package, missing file receipts, then HOLD ALL.

benchmark.text: Benchmark R0 (method): one builder chat (G3, 6ada4669) gave the Owner a locally runnable CII branch editor in about 7 h; Owner estimate for the multi-agent route 40+ h and 5 agents

checklist: Is the Owner's user outcome explicit?
Can the learner try a first working slice?
Are agent count and review gates proportional to risk?
Are changes landing in small integrated PRs?
Does user evidence support the claimed improvement?

items.title: Outcome-led Oracle: build, observe, correct, carry forward
items.summary: Deliver a real inspectable artifact; challenge consequential assumptions; fix contradictions and preserve runnable continuity.
items.aim: Build a usable engineering editor/converter while preserving real input artifacts and validated prior capabilities.
items.observation: Converter and transfer iterations exposed ambiguous branch identity, preview-versus-Apply confusion, raw edit side effects, and insufficiently qualified integration evidence.
items.takeaway: Inspect source and actual behavior → contribute or delegate one bounded slice → falsify → correct → integrate → preserve exact continuation.

recoveries.title: Geometry resemblance is not identity
recoveries.problem: Multiple branches shared plausible geometry even when line IDs differed.
recoveries.correction: Block blind auto-transfer; require explicit identity acceptance bound to revisions.

recoveries.title: Preview is not Apply
recoveries.problem: Audit said applied:false; target output stayed unchanged despite planned changes.
recoveries.correction: Execute Apply explicitly, correct UI labels and prevent misleading export.

recoveries.title: Global replacement contaminated a baseline
recoveries.problem: Find-and-replace in raw CII could change records outside the target branch.
recoveries.correction: Use controlled fixtures, preserve untouched input and compare full field/byte scope.

recoveries.title: Mock UI is not authentic integration
recoveries.problem: Standalone UI tests did not establish actual engineering backend transfer.
recoveries.correction: Recover original pinned backend and test HTTP, export and native browser separately.

stages.title: P1 — Independent typed converter
stages.action: Build a converter and test byte-preserving no-edit roundtrips.
stages.evidence: Contributor self-test; no independent review claim.

stages.title: P2 — Bounded branch transfer
stages.action: Add whole-line T1/P1 transfer behind a mode while preserving original editor.

stages.title: P2.1 — Candidate discovery
stages.action: Experiment with signatures; retain ambiguity rather than treating geometry as identity.

stages.title: P2.1 — Approval and freshness
stages.action: Distinguish Candidate, Accepted, Transfer-ready; bind to document revision.

stages.title: P2.1 — Export contradiction
stages.action: Inspect applied:false and reproduce Preview versus Apply; repair labeling/export gating.
stages.evidence: Owner screen plus bounded reproduced correction.

stages.title: P2.5-A — Workspace UI
stages.action: Keep presentation-only layouts distinct from engineering connector semantics.

stages.title: P2.5-B — Actual backend integration
stages.action: Recover pinned original backend and distinguish mock tests from real HTTP checks.
stages.evidence: Agent-reported backend checks; native browser Owner acceptance outstanding.

rules: Deliver a useful scoped slice before building coordination machinery.
A minimal proof or reproduced failure can prevent ambiguous delegation.
Oracle retains integration accountability and pins exact baseline and next test.
Plausible geometry requires explicit identity judgment.
Candidate is not authorized; Preview does not mutate input.
Mutation must invalidate stale whole-target-document approvals.
Parser, mock, API and served-browser checks establish different claims.
Engineering changes justify stronger checking than throwaway presentation experiments.

cases.title: Outcome beats orchestration
cases.scenario: An Owner asks for a runnable branch editor; a coordinator proposes five new agents, three protocols and extensive tracking before any editable UI exists.
cases.contrast: Create infrastructure first vs build a small working editor preserving original input.
cases.expected_decision: Name the first user-visible capability, bound a runnable vertical slice, implement or delegate it, and keep optional coordination proportional.
cases.discriminating_test: Demonstrate that the Owner can select a fictional branch and preview one field edit in a local application; a plan-only reply fails this claim.
cases.evidence_limit: Usable local UI self-test is not evidence of engineering file fidelity.

cases.title: Candidate is not identity
cases.scenario: Target line IDs differ. Two target branches share the same element lengths, diameter and wall thickness as one source branch.
cases.contrast: Auto-transfer to the first geometry match vs preserve two ambiguous candidates and seek owner acceptance.
cases.expected_decision: Do not authorize a transfer. Show ambiguity and require explicit one-to-one identity acceptance; block splits/merges.
cases.discriminating_test: Construct a second identical-geometry line and confirm the automatic resolver no longer yields transfer-ready.
cases.evidence_limit: Geometry equality is evidence of resemblance only.

cases.title: Accepted mapping becomes stale
cases.scenario: Two line pairs are accepted on the same whole-target XML hash. Apply modifies the first target branch.
cases.contrast: Keep second connector ready vs invalidate old approval.
cases.expected_decision: Mark the second accepted mapping stale, block Apply and require revalidation/reapproval against the new document revision.
cases.discriminating_test: Apply pair A then attempt B with its original acceptance; server must reject without silently resealing.
cases.evidence_limit: A UI badge is insufficient; check backend rejection.

cases.title: Preview is not Apply
cases.scenario: Transfer preview shows 3 planned temperature changes and READY; audit contains applied=false and before/after target hashes are identical. Owner says output did not change.
cases.contrast: Blame converter or user vs inspect plan status and reproduce Apply separately.
cases.expected_decision: Explain that preview did not mutate data; execute an explicit Apply; repair misleading before/after labeling and gate export during pending preview.
cases.discriminating_test: Preview leaves exported bytes unchanged; Apply changes exactly 3 fictional T1 cells, and audit applied=true.
cases.evidence_limit: Field-level diff required; count/size alone does not establish correct edit.

cases.title: Global edit contaminates target
cases.scenario: Owner manually replaces a common temperature string throughout a CII file while intending to change one branch.
cases.contrast: Assume only chosen branch changed vs compare against untouched baseline.
cases.expected_decision: Count and localize all changed records, warn about unintended global edits, and build clean renumber-only fixture separately.
cases.discriminating_test: A byte/field diff reveals changes outside the target branch even if the user selected a correct mapping later.
cases.evidence_limit: Never blame transfer logic for unrelated preexisting edits.

cases.title: Mock UI versus real backend
cases.scenario: Standalone interface and mock browser tests pass, but no authentic engineering backend was available to the successor.
cases.contrast: Call transfer verified vs stage the UI honestly and recover pinned backend.
cases.expected_decision: Label stage as mock-tested, preserve files, recover exact baseline hashes, run actual HTTP and export tests, retain browser NOT_RUN when blocked.
cases.discriminating_test: Unmocked Apply+convert response must produce expected edited CII; a mock fetch must not satisfy this test.
cases.evidence_limit: Authentic API path still does not establish native-browser operation.

cases.title: Contributor or reviewer?
cases.scenario: Oracle authors an adapter and runs 94 tests, then announces that another reviewer has verified it.
cases.contrast: Promote self-test to independent review vs disclose shared authorship.
cases.expected_decision: Label results SELF-TESTED, retain exact tested versions and add independent falsification only when the risk or acceptance process requires it.
cases.discriminating_test: Check test author, expectation lineage and actual candidate access; a separate name alone does not guarantee independence.
cases.evidence_limit: Independence cannot be retroactively created by renaming the agent.

cases.title: Handoff must carry executable state
cases.scenario: Successor can see only a generic prompt, not the frozen backend ZIP; an earlier local conversation has the exact baseline.
cases.contrast: Rebuild P2.1 from description vs recover and pin the original artifact.
cases.expected_decision: Recover the file from authorized custody, verify its hash, include exact API and continuation instructions, and preserve successor implementation.
cases.discriminating_test: Extract exact baseline and execute protected tests before integrating; do not swap another artifact with a similar filename.
cases.evidence_limit: Baseline availability removes a blocker but does not certify new P2.5 integration.

cases.title: Match controls to failure consequence
cases.scenario: A personal prototype needs a useful display. A separate project edits confidential engineering values. The agent proposes identical release gates for both.
cases.contrast: Apply a universal rigid process vs keep aim and tier verification to consequence.
cases.expected_decision: Deliver a usable small UI without excessive ceremony, while requiring field-level negative tests and explicit engineering approval for confidential model edits.
cases.discriminating_test: Ask which plausible failure matters in each use and require only the evidence needed for that claim.
cases.evidence_limit: Proportionality does not excuse mislabeling unsupported PASS.

checklist: Which original artifacts and prior behavior must survive?
Which plausible wrong solution passes a superficial test?
What exact version and claim does each test establish?
Can a successor reproduce the next step without guessing?
items.evidenceLimit: Owner confirmed a corrected P2.1 flow on Windows; later real backend transfer checks were agent-reported. Native served-browser Owner acceptance was still outstanding.
